questions: Does line_loss_events fall to 0 with mass 0.5 kg, or does one loss per run remain?
Does max_error move below about 0.06 m, or does it stay pinned at the off-track floor? If pinned, is the limit lag or steering authority?
Does steering_oscillation stay below about 0.2 with lower yaw inertia, or does the robot now overshoot the bends?
If line losses are gone but progress is still low, is the limit now top speed, so that a wheel_radius increase to 0.035 m is the next step?

intent: Test whether lower mass (0.7 to 0.5 kg, about 29 percent less yaw inertia) clears the single line-loss event per run that persisted through pitch and footprint changes. Only mass changes from the iteration 3 design, so the result is attributable. Expected result: line_loss_events fall toward 0 and max_error drops below about 0.06 m. If both happen, the next step is to test forward offset y = 0.06 m for lead. If line losses persist, the next step is to test a wheel_radius increase for top speed.
learning: Iterations 0 to 3 show that sensor pitch (10, 15, 20 mm), footprint (12 to 16 mm), and track width (0.12 to 0.10 m) do not change max_error or the one line-loss event per run. The next iteration isolates mass, the only remaining untested variable that affects yaw inertia. If mass also fails, the limit is likely lag (forward offset) or top speed (wheel radius), and those should be tested one at a time.
rationale: Evidence from iterations 0 to 3: all 240 trials ended off_track. max_error sits at the 0.060 to 0.067 m off-track floor, and progress is only 0.10 to 0.18. Line_loss_events stayed at 1 per run on every track after the footprint change to 0.016 m (iteration 3), so coverage at 0.016 m did not remove the line loss. Steering_oscillation is low (0.07 to 0.16), so the robot drifts steadily rather than oscillating. Sensor pitch (10, 15, 20 mm), track narrowing to 0.10 m, and footprint (0.012 to 0.016 m) have each failed to move max_error, so none of these is the binding lever. The Robot Integrator's contingency rule, written for this candidate, says that if line losses persist at 1 per run with the 0.016 m footprint, do not widen the pitch further, and try mass 0.5 kg to reduce yaw inertia. The yaw inertia formula (mass*(L²+W²)/12) gives a direct reduction of about 29 percent from 0.7 to 0.5 kg. I therefore keep the iteration 3 geometry (0.016 m footprint, 20 mm pitch at x = -0.04 to +0.04, y = 0.04, track 0.10 m, wheel radius 0.03 m, body 0.18 x 0.12 m) and change only mass, from 0.7 to 0.5 kg. Expected result: a smaller yaw inertia lets the robot turn back toward the line sooner, so line_loss_events should fall, ideally to 0, and max_error should drop below about 0.06 m. I expect progress to stay low, because top speed is not yet limited by the design. The off-track floor cannot be raised, since body_width does not lift it above 0.06 m in range.
